563	    def _revalidate_for_append(self):
564	        """Validate the whole log by the exact recover rules before appending.
565	
566	        A store can stay open while its log is appended to or damaged out of
567	        band, so the boundaries cached when the store opened are never trusted
568	        for a write: the log is replayed from the head exactly as recover()
569	        does, re-determining valid_bytes, committed_bytes, and the last
570	        committed state. The replay builds only local objects, so a terminated
571	        invalid record, a blank/whitespace record, illegal UTF-8, duplicate or
572	        missing fields, an unknown op, a bad key/value, or a seq break raises
573	        WalCorruptionError without appending, truncating, or adopting anything
574	        -- state, commit_seq, and the byte boundary a later rollback observes
575	        are all left untouched.
576	
577	        The only bytes allowed beyond the replayed valid_bytes are the single
578	        trailing interrupted-write fragment the recovery rules recognise; that
579	        fragment is removed in place exactly as before, while every complete
580	        record before it -- legal uncommitted set/delete records included -- is
581	        preserved byte for byte. Returns the replayed committed view and the
582	        last committed seq in the file; the next record must use
583	        ``committed + 1`` rather than any seq cached at open time.
584	        """
585	        self.path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
586	        saved_boundary = self._valid_size
587	        try:
588	            (
589	                candidate,
590	                committed,
591	                _pending_count,
592	                valid_size,
593	                _committed_size,
594	            ) = self._replay()
595	            file_size = self.path.stat().st_size if self.path.exists() else 0
596	            if file_size > valid_size:
597	                # The replay has already proved the bytes beyond valid_size
598	                # are exactly one unfinished tail fragment -- anything else
599	                # raised WalCorruptionError above -- so removing them can
600	                # never discard a complete, terminated record.
601	                with self.path.open("r+b") as f:
602	                    self._authorize_write_handle(f)
603	                    f.truncate(valid_size)
604	                    f.flush()
605	                    os.fsync(f.fileno())
606	        except BaseException:
607	            # Neither a failed validation nor a failed fragment removal
608	            # adopts a boundary: state, commit_seq, and the cached
609	            # accepted-prefix edge stay exactly as on entry. Every later
610	            # write revalidates from the head in any case.
611	            self._valid_size = saved_boundary
612	            raise
613	        return candidate, committed

615	    def _append(self, row):
616	        """Durably append one log record after head-to-tail revalidation.
617	
618	        The whole log is validated under the exact recover rules first (see
619	        _revalidate_for_append); WalCorruptionError propagates with the file
620	        and in-memory state untouched. The record's seq is stamped from the
621	        seq replayed out of the file -- the file's last committed seq plus
622	        one -- never from a value cached when the store opened, so a batch
623	        committed out of band while the store was open extends the chain
624	        instead of being overwritten.
625	
626	        Raises OSError if the record cannot be written or synced; the
627	        un-durable tail is best-effort truncated back so a failed write can
628	        never masquerade as a committed record on reopen, and no new state is
629	        adopted before the record is durable.
630	        """
631	        candidate, committed = self._revalidate_for_append()
632	        record = dict(row)
633	        record["seq"] = committed + 1
634	        line = json.dumps(record, sort_keys=True) + "\n"
635	        created = not self.path.exists()
636	        with self.path.open("a", encoding="utf-8") as f:
637	            self._authorize_write_handle(f)
638	            saved_size = f.tell()
639	            try:
640	                f.write(line)
641	                f.flush()
642	                os.fsync(f.fileno())
643	            except OSError:
644	                try:
645	                    f.truncate(saved_size)
646	                    f.flush()
647	                    os.fsync(f.fileno())
648	                except OSError:
649	                    pass
650	                raise
651	            new_size = f.tell()
652	        # Adopt only once the appended record is complete and durable.
653	        # candidate is the last *committed* view -- pending records never
654	        # join it -- so a set/delete append keeps the state deferred until
655	        # commit exactly as before, while a batch committed out of band
656	        # converges memory with what a reopen would recover.
657	        self._valid_size = new_size
658	        self.state = candidate
659	        self.commit_seq = committed
660	        if created:
661	            self._fsync_parent_dir()
662	
663	    def _fsync_parent_dir(self):
664	        """Best-effort persistence of a freshly created log file's directory entry."""
665	        try:
666	            fd = os.open(str(self.path.parent), os.O_RDONLY)
667	        except OSError:
668	            return
669	        try:
670	            os.fsync(fd)
671	        except OSError:
672	            # Some filesystems do not support fsync on directories; the log
673	            # contents themselves have already been synced.
674	            pass
675	        finally:
676	            os.close(fd)

693	    def commit(self):

703	    def rollback(self):
704	        # Validate the log by the exact recovery rules before touching
705	        self._check_writable()
706	        # anything. The replay builds only local objects, so corruption raises
707	        # WalCorruptionError without partially replacing state or commit_seq.
708	        # committed_size is the byte offset just past the last commit record;
709	        # every complete set/delete beyond it is the uncommitted batch, and any
710	        # bytes beyond valid_size are the discardable interrupted-write tail.
711	        (
712	            _candidate,
713	            _committed,
714	            pending_count,
715	            _valid_size,
716	            committed_size,
717	        ) = self._replay()
718	        if not self.path.exists() or self.path.stat().st_size <= committed_size:
719	            # Nothing sits beyond the committed prefix (pending_count is then
720	            # necessarily 0); no truncation is needed.
721	            self._valid_size = committed_size
722	            return pending_count
723	        # Shrink the log in place: bytes of the committed prefix are never
724	        # rewritten or reordered, only the tail beyond the last commit is
725	        # removed. Persist before returning, and let an OSError from open,
726	        # truncate, flush, or fsync propagate -- a failed truncation must
727	        # never masquerade as a successful rollback. state and commit_seq are
728	        # not touched: they already equal the last committed view.
729	        with self.path.open("r+b") as f:
730	            self._authorize_write_handle(f)
731	            f.truncate(committed_size)
732	            f.flush()
733	            os.fsync(f.fileno())
734	        self._valid_size = committed_size
735	        return pending_count

737	    def restore(self, target_seq):
738	        """Commit the state of a past commit boundary as a fresh new state.
739	
740	        Read-only with respect to history: no earlier record is rewritten
741	        or reordered, and snapshot/history still serve every old commit.
742	        The target state is reached by one new set/delete batch sealed by
743	        one new commit, whose seq is latest commit_seq + 1 even when the
744	        target equals the current state (an empty batch then) or is 0
745	        (an empty state). Returns the new commit_seq.
746	
747	        target_seq must be a non-boolean non-negative integer no greater
748	        than the latest committed seq; type errors, negatives, and
749	        out-of-range values raise ValueError before the log is touched.
750	        The log is then validated under the exact recover/snapshot rules
751	        (corruption anywhere raises WalCorruptionError), and must be
752	        settled at the last commit: complete uncommitted set/delete
753	        records or a trailing unfinished fragment make it raise
754	        WalPendingError with the file, state, and commit_seq untouched.
755	        Every change record and the commit are appended and fsynced one
756	        at a time as in set/commit; an OSError propagates with the old
757	        committed state and seq in place, already-written records simply
758	        forming the batch's pending tail (rollback clears them).
759	        """
760	        self._check_writable()
761	        if (
762	            isinstance(target_seq, bool)
763	            or not isinstance(target_seq, int)
764	            or target_seq < 0
765	        ):
766	            raise ValueError(
767	                "target_seq must be a non-negative integer, got %r"
768	                % (target_seq,)
769	            )
770	        # Full recover/snapshot validation first, purely into local
771	        # objects: corruption raises before any truncation or append.
772	        history_views = []
773	        candidate, committed, pending_count, _valid_size, _committed_size = (
774	            self._replay(snapshots=history_views)
775	        )
776	        if target_seq > committed:
777	            raise ValueError(
778	                "target_seq %r exceeds latest committed seq %r"
779	                % (target_seq, committed)
780	            )
781	        # The log must be settled: neither a complete, terminated
782	        # uncommitted batch nor an unfinished tail fragment may be spliced
783	        # into. A tail fragment is recover/audit-recognised garbage the
784	        # next append would truncate away; refusing here keeps restore
785	        # from appending (or truncating) anything before validation has
786	        # fully passed, and forces the caller to commit, rollback, or
787	        # repair explicitly.
788	        file_size = self.path.stat().st_size if self.path.exists() else 0
789	        if pending_count > 0 or file_size > self._valid_size:
790	            raise WalPendingError(
791	                "log is not settled at commit %r: %r pending record(s), "
792	                "an unfinished tail fragment is present"
793	                % (committed, pending_count)
794	            )
795	        current = candidate
796	        target = {} if target_seq == 0 else dict(history_views)[target_seq]
797	        # Merge the two key sets and write deterministically in Unicode
798	        # (code point) key order. A key only in the target, or present
799	        # with a different value under JSON-type-aware comparison, is a
800	        # set; a key present now but absent in the target is a delete.
801	        new_seq = committed + 1
802	        for key in sorted(set(current) | set(target)):
803	            if key not in target:
804	                self._append({"op": "delete", "key": key, "seq": new_seq})
805	            elif key not in current or not _json_equal(current[key], target[key]):
806	                # Deep copy: the adopted value must not share objects with
807	                # the replay's snapshot, which the caller could mutate.
808	                self._append(
809	                    {
810	                        "op": "set",
811	                        "key": key,
812	                        "value": copy.deepcopy(target[key]),
813	                        "seq": new_seq,
814	                    }
815	                )
816	        self._append({"op": "commit", "seq": new_seq})
817	        # Adopt the new committed view only once its commit boundary is
818	        # durable, exactly as commit() does.
819	        self.recover()
820	        return self.commit_seq

822	    def apply_batch(self, base_seq, changes):

825	        Every change is appended to the log first, in the caller's order,
826	        and the batch is sealed by one new commit record whose seq is the
827	        latest committed seq + 1 -- exactly as if the caller had issued the
828	        same set/delete records one at a time and then committed. Returns
829	        the new commit_seq. An empty changes collection is an empty commit:
830	        no change records, one commit record, seq advancing by one.
831	
832	        base_seq is the caller-declared compare-and-swap precondition: it
833	        must be a non-boolean non-negative integer and must equal the log's
834	        latest committed seq, otherwise the call raises ValueError or the
835	        unique WalConflictError respectively. Each change must be a dict
836	        carrying exactly the existing record semantics -- {"op": "set",
837	        "key", "value"} or {"op": "delete", "key"} -- with a string key and
838	        a value under the existing JSON-compatibility rules; any other
839	        shape raises ValueError. All argument validation completes before
840	        the log is touched.
841	
842	        The log is then validated under the exact recover rules (any
843	        corruption raises WalCorruptionError) and must be settled at the
844	        last commit: complete uncommitted set/delete records or a
845	        recover/audit-recognisable unfinished tail fragment raise
846	        WalPendingError. None of these rejections writes, truncates, or
847	        alters in-memory state. A read-only instance raises
848	        WalReadOnlyError and a closed one WalClosedError before any of the
849	        above, exactly as the other mutating entries do.
850	
851	        The write phase follows the same single-writer lease, per-record
852	        flush+fsync, and seq monotonicity rules as set/delete/commit: an
853	        OSError from any change record or the final commit propagates
854	        unchanged, the already-durable prefix stays observable through
855	        pending_changes and removable through rollback, and neither the
856	        in-memory state nor commit_seq advances. A process terminated at
857	        any write boundary recovers to the last complete commit on reopen;
858	        the unsealed part of the batch is never applied. Values are
859	        deep-copied into the written records, so neither the caller's
860	        changes collection nor the returned seq shares mutable nested
861	        objects with the store.
862	        """
863	        self._check_writable()
864	        if (
865	            isinstance(base_seq, bool)
866	            or not isinstance(base_seq, int)
867	            or base_seq < 0
868	        ):
869	            raise ValueError(
870	                "base_seq must be a non-negative integer, got %r" % (base_seq,)
871	            )
872	        if not isinstance(changes, (list, tuple)):
873	            raise ValueError(
874	                "changes must be a list of change records, got %r"
875	                % (type(changes).__name__,)
876	            )
877	        # Validate and normalize every change up front: a rejected call
878	        # must never create, truncate, or append to the log or alter
879	        # in-memory state. Values are deep-copied so the written records
880	        # can never share mutable nested objects with the caller's
881	        # collection.
882	        normalized = []
883	        for index, change in enumerate(changes):
884	            if not isinstance(change, dict):
885	                raise ValueError(
886	                    "change %r must be a dict, got %r"
887	                    % (index, type(change).__name__)
888	                )
889	            op = change.get("op")
890	            if op == "set":
891	                if set(change) != {"op", "key", "value"}:
892	                    raise ValueError(
893	                        "set change %r must carry exactly op, key and value, "
894	                        "got %r" % (index, sorted(change))
895	                    )
896	                _validate_key(change["key"])
897	                _validate_value(change["value"])
898	                normalized.append(
899	                    {
900	                        "op": "set",
901	                        "key": change["key"],
902	                        "value": copy.deepcopy(change["value"]),
903	                    }
904	                )
905	            elif op == "delete":
906	                if set(change) != {"op", "key"}:
907	                    raise ValueError(
908	                        "delete change %r must carry exactly op and key, "
909	                        "got %r" % (index, sorted(change))
910	                    )
911	                _validate_key(change["key"])
912	                normalized.append({"op": "delete", "key": change["key"]})
913	            else:
914	                raise ValueError(
915	                    "change %r has unknown op %r: only 'set' and 'delete' "
916	                    "records may be batched" % (index, op)
917	                )
918	        # Full recover-rule validation of the log, purely into local
919	        # objects: corruption raises WalCorruptionError before anything is
920	        # written, truncated, or adopted.
921	        (
922	            _candidate,
923	            committed,
924	            pending_count,
925	            _valid_size,
926	            _committed_size,
927	        ) = self._replay()
928	        # The log must be settled at the last commit before a new batch is
929	        # spliced on: neither complete uncommitted records nor a
930	        # recognisable unfinished tail fragment may be present (same rule
931	        # as restore).
932	        file_size = self.path.stat().st_size if self.path.exists() else 0
933	        if pending_count > 0 or file_size > self._valid_size:
934	            raise WalPendingError(
935	                "log is not settled at commit %r: %r pending record(s), "
936	                "an unfinished tail fragment is present"
937	                % (committed, pending_count)
938	            )
939	        if base_seq != committed:
940	            raise WalConflictError(
941	                "base_seq %r does not match latest committed seq %r"
942	                % (base_seq, committed)
943	            )

947	        # already-written records form the batch's pending tail.
948	        new_seq = committed + 1
949	        for change in normalized:
950	            record = dict(change)
951	            record["seq"] = new_seq
952	            self._append(record)
953	        self._append({"op": "commit", "seq": new_seq})
954	        # Adopt the new committed view only once its commit boundary is
955	        # durable, exactly as commit() does.
956	        self.recover()

990	    def scan(self, start_key=None, end_key=None, limit=None):
991	        """Read-only deterministic range scan of the last committed view.
992	
993	        Returns the committed items whose keys lie in the half-open range
994	        [start_key, end_key), sorted by Unicode code point and capped at
995	        limit items; each item is exactly {"key": key, "value": value} with
996	        an independent deep copy of the value. An omitted bound means
997	        unbounded on that side, an omitted limit means no cap, and a zero
998	        limit returns an empty list. With no matching keys -- including a
999	        missing or empty log -- the result is an empty list and no file is
1000	        created.
1001	
1002	        start_key and end_key must each be a string or omitted, start_key
1003	        must not exceed end_key, and limit must be a non-boolean
1004	        non-negative integer (or omitted); every such rejection is a
1005	        ValueError raised before the log is read. The whole log is then
1006	        validated under the exact recover rules: corruption anywhere --
1007	        the committed region, terminated uncommitted records, or an
1008	        unrecognisable tail -- raises WalCorruptionError with no partial
1009	        result, while a single trailing interrupted-write fragment is
1010	        ignored by the recover rules. Uncommitted set/delete records are
1011	        never visible: only the state of the last complete commit is
1012	        served.
1013	
1014	        The scan never appends, truncates, or rewrites the log and never
1015	        changes state, commit_seq, pending_count, or the cached
1016	        accepted-prefix boundary; a read-only instance scans without
1017	        taking the write lease and an exclusive instance keeps its lease
1018	        untouched. Repeated scans of the same acceptable log prefix,
